correctness.rationale: The planar support-function area formula gives D_0=(π/2)Σ_{m>=2}(m²−1)(a_m²+b_m²); it is valid for nonsmooth convex bodies via W^{1,2} approximation. Independent Haar-uniform reflection axes become i.i.d. first-angle/successive-difference variables. Each m-th Fourier weight is multiplied by cos² of its projected angle, giving mean 1/2, fourth moment 3/8 and cross-mode second moment 1/4. Tonelli justifies summing countably many nonnegative finite-total weights; thus Var(D_t)=((3/8)^t−4^{-t})Q and Cov(D_s,D_t)=2^{-(t−s)}Var(D_s). Q<=D0² with equality exactly one active higher harmonic. M_t=2^tD_t is a nonnegative martingale; for each fixed mode E log(2cos²(mU))=−log2, so it decays almost surely; the limit of all remaining tail martingales has mean at most the initial discarded Fourier-tail sum and hence tends to zero. Independent 256x256 angle quadrature on three Fourier modes matched two-step mean and variance exactly to numerical tolerance, but the general statement is analytic.

value.rationale: PASS: Exact time-covariance of a natural intrinsic isoperimetric statistic, sharp geometric single-harmonic variance extremizers and an almost-sure decay vastly faster than mean are distinct useful mathematical conclusions. This refines known expected contraction in a highly interpretable stochastic-geometric model.

limitations: Only planar Minkowski, uniform independent reflection axes and perimeter-preserving deficit; not Steiner/nonuniform/high dimensional.
Nonsmooth case relies on standard weak support-area identity; finite quadrature does not prove general theorem.
